editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks Set Theory 3.7 opening definitions. It distinguishes unbounded/cofinal subsets of a well-ordered set from ordinal cofinality, which measures the least order type of such subsets.

definitions.text: A subset A of a well-ordered set T is cofinal if for every t∈T some a∈A satisfies t≤a.
definitions.context_hint: Order theory: cofinal subset of a well-order

definitions.text: For an ordinal α, its cofinality cf(α) is the least ordinal that is order-isomorphic to a cofinal subset of α; equivalently cf(α) is the smallest cardinality of a cofinal subset.
definitions.context_hint: Set theory: cofinality of an ordinal

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.8, Definition 10.8.1 and Lemmas 10.8.2–10.8.3. They construct directed systems and colimits of modules, including a quotient of the direct sum by compatibility relations.

definitions.text: A system of R-modules indexed by a preordered set I consists of modules M_i and maps μ_ij:M_i→M_j whenever i≤j with μ_ii=id and μ_ik=μ_jk∘μ_ij; it is directed if I is directed.
definitions.context_hint: Module theory: direct system of modules

definitions.text: The colimit of a diagram (M_i,μ_ij) of R-modules is the quotient of the direct sum ⊕_i M_i by the submodule generated by all elements ι_i(m)−ι_j(μ_ij(m)) for i≤j.

Inspected Stacks Categories 4.11, Definition 4.11.1. It defines a coequalizer of parallel arrows by an initial universal factorization among arrows that identify the two composites.

definitions.text: For parallel arrows f,g:X⇉Y in a category C, a coequalizer is a morphism q:Y→Q with qf=qg such that every h:Y→Z satisfying hf=hg factors uniquely as h=u q for a morphism u:Q→Z.

definitions.text: An element α of a field extension E/F is algebraic over F if some nonzero polynomial f∈F[x] satisfies f(α)=0.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: algebraic element over a field

definitions.text: A field extension E/F is algebraic if every element of E satisfies at least one nonzero polynomial with coefficients in F.

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.6, Definition 10.6.1, defining finite-type and finitely presented ring homomorphisms by finite generators and the stronger condition of finitely generated polynomial relations.

definitions.text: A ring map R→S is of finite type if S can be generated as an R-algebra by finitely many elements, equivalently S is a quotient of R[x_1,…,x_n] for some finite n.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: ring homomorphism of finite type

definitions.text: A ring map R→S is of finite presentation if S is R-isomorphic to R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m) for finite families of polynomial generators and relations.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: finitely presented ring homomorphism

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.104, Definitions 10.104.1 and 10.104.6. They distinguish Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local rings by a depth equality and general Cohen–Macaulay rings by requiring the property at each localization.

definitions.text: A Noetherian local ring (R,m) is Cohen–Macaulay if its depth as an R-module equals its Krull dimension, that is, depth_m(R)=dim(R).
A Noetherian commutative ring R is Cohen–Macaulay if for every maximal or prime ideal p, the local ring R_p is Cohen–Macaulay.

Inspected Stacks Topology 5.23, Definition 5.23.1 and the subsequent construction of constructible topology. Spectral spaces and spectral maps are distinct object types; the constructible topology is a separate topology generated by compact-open sets and complements.

definitions.text: A space X is spectral if it is sober and quasi-compact, intersections of two quasi-compact open sets are quasi-compact, and the quasi-compact opens form a basis for the topology.
A continuous map f:X→Y between spectral spaces is spectral if inverse images of quasi-compact open sets in Y are quasi-compact in X.
For a spectral space X, the constructible topology is generated by the quasi-compact open subsets of X together with their complements; these sets constitute a subbasis.
definitions.source_section: Section 5.23 constructible topology paragraph after Definition 5.23.1
definitions.context_hint: Topology: constructible or patch topology of a spectral space

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.24, Lemma 10.24.1 and Lemma 10.24.5. The section describes compatible local sections and module gluing data on a finite standard-open cover with cocycle conditions, providing a precise descent construction.

definitions.text: For elements f_1,…,f_n∈R generating the unit ideal and an R-module M, a compatible family of local sections is a tuple (m_i∈M_{f_i}) whose images agree in M_{f_i f_j} for every pair i,j; such tuples are exactly the image of M under its diagonal localization map.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: gluing compatible sections on standard opens

definitions.text: For a cover of Spec(R) by D(f_i), gluing data for modules comprise R_{f_i}-modules M_i and isomorphisms between their localizations over D(f_i f_j), satisfying identity and triple-overlap cocycle conditions.
definitions.context_hint: Module theory: descent data over a finite affine open cover
